issue_body:
Hi,
I am using .creation.sweep_polygon with a shapely polygon as input for the "polygon" parameter. The function does create extrusion shapes, however, I am having trouble understanding the orientation of the polygon when sweeping along the extrusion path. Shapely polygons only have x,y coordinates, that's fine, but how are these axes then re-oriented in 3D space for the extrusion with sweep_polygon, when the extrusion path is not aligned in z-direction ? Maybe I am missing something obvious here, but I have had surprising results when trying to work it out myself.
trimesh.creation.sweep_polygon - sweep without banking?
As I understand it, the sweep_polygon function rotates the polygon along x when it sweeps along a 3Dpath. In other software this is usually called banking when sweeping objects along a path. See here:
https://www.cadforum.cz/en/what-for-is-the-bank-option-of-the-sweep-command-tip12471

Is it possible to not rotate the polygon along X when sweeping? I would like resulting trimesh not to be banked.
Examples with a swept rectangle:
![2D](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10772529/145786168-3b8cdc26-7daf-4146-99c7-20937e3b1b68.png)
![banked](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10772529/145786180-3ec64de1-7e48-41a1-84d1-c9168dac3017.jpg)
![not_banked](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10772529/145786188-1392f324-a32e-49b8-8621-e5a3605bbbae.jpg)


I tried setting the angles option in trimesh.creation.sweep_polygon to a list with 0.0 values but it did not have any effect. Do I need calculate the angles for all vertices/line segments in the 3Dpath and then supply that to the angles option? Would appreciate an example if that is the case.

Thanks!
sweep_polygon not a superset of extrude_polygon?
Using trimesh 3.14.1

Something is confusing me in the relationship of sweep_polygon and extrude polygon.
I would have thought that sweeping from [0,0,0] to [0,0,z] would have been the same as extruding z.
However, this is not the case:

```
from shapely import wkt
from trimesh.creation import extrude_polygon, sweep_polygon

wkt_str = 'POLYGON ((5.00377535 -55.9875328200079, 5.00377535 -48.78608924996518, 0.5577428000031441 -48.78608924996518, 0.5577428000031441 -59.109798756658876, 70.78461385999685 -59.109798756658876, 70.78461385999685 -49.54863710000369, 63.648103400000004 -49.54863710000369, 63.648103400000004 -55.9875328200079, 5.00377535 -55.9875328200079))'
poly = wkt.loads(wkt_str)

extruded = extrude_polygon(poly, 5)
sweeped = sweep_polygon(poly, [(0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 5)])

print(poly.bounds)
print(extruded.bounds)
print(sweeped.bounds)
```

outputs this:

```
(0.5577428000031441, -59.109798756658876, 70.78461385999685, -48.78608924996518)
[[  0.5577428  -59.10979876   0.        ]
 [ 70.78461386 -48.78608925   5.        ]]
[[ 0.5577428  48.78608925  0.        ]
 [70.78461386 59.10979876  5.        ]]
```

It looks like the Y coordinate is flipped in sweep_polygon. How come?
Issue loading .STEP files using Gmsh
I was following this thread (https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/issues/945), and it worked well for me, however, gmsh keeps writing new stl files to a a directory on my system. They all begin with tmp.....stl. Is there a way to prevent this or at least change the directory?
sweep_polygon with cyclic path
Hello there. First let me thank you for such great library!

I'm looking for making a path extrude like sweep_polygon where path is actually a closed shape (the beginning of the path is the same as the end). I've tried using the function and it works fine, but not for cyclic path, it stays open at the end. By looking at the code I see the "cap" at beginning and and are created and I see no option to remove them and close the shape. Would that be an interesting feature to develop add a flag for that use case (I could contribute)? Or maybe I missed a function doing this already.

funny example: from svg (red one is the profile=polygon and blue one is the cyclic path) into a mesh ![image](https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/assets/2393097/492af238-b4a6-4f50-9b38-2fd152cf0104)

Thank you.
Instability with normal generation with trimesh.creation.sweep_polygon
I have been using the `trimesh.creation.sweep_polygon `with the following path:

```
path = array([[38.10477237, 21.67300341,  7.94233277],
                       [38.10477237, 21.67299835,  6.94233277],
                       [38.10477237, 21.67299688,  6.65233277],
                       [37.89523014, 20.84123975,  4.53453201]])

trimesh.creation.sweep_polygon(poly, path)
```

As a result,  It took a while to diagnose the issue internally to the function. I have noticed there are instabilities with the generation of the normals that are created across the path. In this situation the X-coordinate is kept the same, and the y coordinates are numerically very close. Generating the path will results in vertices that are extremely large, due to normals having small components.

I don't know which method you are using to construct the paths along the curve. Hopefully, you can investigate the instability?

Many thanks,
Luke 
GMSH stops on module 'gmsh' has no attribute 'isInitialized'. 
Hey. I'm trying to get gmsh to work to import a step file. However, this simple code does not work:

`import numpy as np`
`import trimesh`
`trimesh.util.attach_to_log()`
`mesh = trimesh.interfaces.gmsh.load_gmsh('trimesh/models/BREP/base_interface_AP203.STEP')`


As it stops on this:

`Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "c:\projects\blenderstl\main.py", line 32, in <module>
    mesh = trimesh.interfaces.gmsh.load_gmsh('trimesh/models/BREP/base_interface_AP203.STEP')
  File "C:\Python310\lib\site-packages\trimesh\interfaces\gmsh.py", line 79, in load_gmsh
    if not gmsh.isInitialized():
AttributeError: module 'gmsh' has no attribute 'isInitialized'. Did you mean: 'initialize'?`

Am I missing something obvious?

hints_text:
Hello,


I'm facing the exact same issue with trimesh version 4.2.3.

Here is an MWE showing the shape's tilt along the 3D path:

```py
import numpy as np
from shapely.geometry import Polygon
from trimesh.creation import sweep_polygon

shape = Polygon([[0, 0],[2, 0], [2, 1], [0, 1], [0, 0]])
path = np.array([
    [  0,  0,  0],
    [  0, 10, 10],
    [ 10, 20, 20],
    [ 30, 20, 20]
])
mesh = sweep_polygon(shape, path)
```
![image](https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/assets/19967599/5ce9e639-5447-43c4-8538-10e8d807a151)

This is mainly due to the fact that the shape is rotated around an axis perpendicular to the plane defined by the two edges of a path at their common vertex.

Hey, `sweep_polygon` isn't as well tested as `extrude_polygon`, this seems likely to just be bug and I agree the behavior of sweep and extrude for a single segment seem like they should be the same. PR's welcome!



Glad it's useful! Yeah I think that case probably isn't handled in sweep (PR's welcome!). You could also try `trimesh.creation.revolve` and then apply a skew if the path is just an elipse. Revolve definitely handles the closed case as it's used for generating all the revolved solids (capsule/cone/cylinder/etc) in trimesh.creation.



https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/blob/c880b028243fdcb128368d9dcd73fdb343fa15ac/trimesh/creation.py#L41-L76
Greetings @mikedh! During the time since posting, I've wrote my own implementation, the reason is I wanted something general that can handle pretty much anything simply. One of my concrete example was making a screw thread. I tried in trimesh and here is what happened (the shape starts at the bottom and goes upwards, we can see the original polygon at beginning, it started so well):

![image](https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/assets/2393097/6721bf20-dcc6-4dc7-903c-a1aafe92da9a)

Basically I specify a path that's a XY circle up to `2*pi*height/pitch` and Z is np.linspace going up (one pitch for each revolution of XY). We can see the sweeped polygon is rotated more and more with every turn (some kind of roll), that's really weird! My implementation doesn't have path pitch yet but has proper orientation, this is what I expected:

![image](https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/assets/2393097/f7213be8-7692-49ab-bed9-f621f47429ff)

Any idea why trimesh does that roll? It seems it wasn't made for rotations >2pi I'm not sure. I tried reading the code but didn't had much time. Maybe you can shed some light on that aspect?

Here is another example I wanted to be able to do: rails along arbitrary path with an arbitrary profile:
![image](https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/assets/2393097/0ead27f5-c223-400d-9347-683b74d622f2)

Depending if the incremental roll exhibited above by trimesh is part of its feature (for some reason it escapes me right now), if not I may be able to adapt it to make a PR in trimesh then we can assess if it's useful to contribute. Also I'm sorry I don't have the trimesh code at hand but I can provide it or try rewriting it quickly if necessary (let me know). Thoughts?


PS: I was curious so I've given a shot with revolve but it's closing the top surface (which doesn't make sense to me because the profile shape isn't wide enough to close it). Left is revolve and right is mine I remade:

![image](https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh/assets/2393097/53b1838f-8c02-4f5f-8688-06bbbdfc9c92)


Actually I was able to isolate my code into something standalone:

```python
#!/usr/bin/python
import numpy as np
from numpy import array as V
import math
from trimesh.exchange.export import export_mesh
from trimesh.creation import sweep_polygon
from shapely.geometry import Polygon

def arc_2d(final_angle, d=1, start_angle=0, splits=20):
    xs = np.linspace(start_angle, final_angle, splits)
    return np.stack((d/2 * np.cos(xs), d/2 * np.sin(xs)), axis=1)

h=200
d=8
h1=1
w = 2
d = d - w
h2 = h1

lead = 2
splits_per_turn = 4*20

polygon = V([(-0.01, -h1/2),
             (w, -h2/2),
             (w, +h2/2),
             (-0.01, +h1/2)])

h_ = h + h1
n = math.ceil(splits_per_turn * h_ / lead)
turns = n / splits_per_turn
xys = arc_2d(2*np.pi * turns, d, splits=n)
zs = np.linspace(0, h_, n)[:,None]
spin_path = np.concatenate((xys, zs), axis=1)

x = sweep_polygon(Polygon(polygon), spin_path)

export_mesh(x, 'screw_test_trimesh.stl')
```

Although it's not exactly the same screw as in the screenshot above, it exhibits the same "roll" behavior. Hope this helps.
